questions.stem: In an ideal transformer, if the voltage is stepped up by a factor of 10, what happens to the current?

options.text: The current also increases by a factor of 10
The current decreases by a factor of 10

questions.explanation: In an ideal transformer, power in equals power out (VpIp = VsIs). If the voltage increases by a factor of 10, the current must decrease by a factor of 10 to keep the power constant. This is why high-voltage transmission uses low current.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a source of energy loss in a real transformer?

options.text: Eddy currents in the iron core
Electromagnetic induction in the secondary coil

questions.explanation: Electromagnetic induction in the secondary coil is the desired function of the transformer, not a source of energy loss. The actual losses include resistance heating in the coils, eddy currents in the core, magnetic flux leakage, and hysteresis losses.
